thread:
alex: Heads-up: acme-inc reported a sharp p95 token latency spike yesterday ~22:10 UTC. Datadog alert attached. Sampling shows a lot of short sequences but very high token tail. Anyone seen this pattern tied to kernel selection or tiny batch windows?

datadog-bot: Alert: token_latency.p95 > 350ms (workspace=acme-inc, model=redwood-phi-7b-q4). See: https://dd.example/alert/XYZ123

maya: I'm poking at traces now. Most of the hot traces got routed to `matmul_v2` instead of `matmul_fused` even when seq_len > 256. Batching window dropped to ~8ms around the spike so effective batch_size=2-3.

jamal: Is that routing deterministic? Could be kernel selector using stale perf profile. We only collect kernel selection telemetry globally today, not by workspace/route, so it's hard to prove tenant causality.

linh: I ran a quick kv-cache probe against acme-inc traffic sample. Hit rate ~12% vs expected ~50-60% for similar workloads. Their request shapes have lots of short unique prefixes -> cache partitioning looks noisy.

alex: So two hypotheses: (1) tiny batches + wrong kernel variant -> per-token overheads, (2) poor KV cache locality for this tenant increasing per-token compute. We should surface both in tenant-level metrics.

maya: Agreed. Proposal: add per-workspace breakdowns for token_latency (p50/p95/p99), batch_size distribution, kernel_variant counts, and kv_cache_hit_rate. Also include a small-sample trace link per datapoint.

jamal: +1. Also need RBAC: product wants only tenant owners/ops to view other org panels. We should implement workspace-scoped dashboards (templated panels + team-level perms) rather than one jumbo global dashboard.

linh: Quick config note: acme-inc is on dedicated nodes with `kernel_hint: auto`. The runtime fallback switches to `matmul_v2` when measured batch_size < 4 due to throughput heuristics. Maybe we need a heuristic that prefers fused kernels for seq_len >= 256 even for small batches.

maya: I can prototype a `kernel_hint_policy: prefer_fused_for_seq_ge=256` toggle and run a canary. If fused has better tail even at batch=2 it'll help p95. We should only roll to 10% traffic initially.

alex: Good. For dashboards I'll mock a Grafana folder: panels -> token_lat_by_workspace, kernel_variant_heatmap, batch_size_hist, kv_hit_rate_timeseries, trace_sample_links. Will add template var `workspace` and a top-level RBAC filter. Draft link: https://grafana.internal/d/redwood/tenant-perf-metrics (WIP)

jamal: Action items: 1) alex -> dashboard PR + RBAC scoping; 2) maya -> runtime kernel_hint PR + canary plan; 3) linh -> kv cache partition audit + sampling probe; 4) jamal -> add per-workspace metric tags and wire kernel_variant tag to token latency metric.

alex: I'll open the PRs now and add checklists. ETA: dashboards + tags by EOD tomorrow.

maya: I'll schedule canary for acme-inc dedicated nodes, 10% traffic, monitor p95 and kv hit delta.

linh: Putting a quick probe command here that I used: `./kvprobe --workspace acme-inc --sample 5000 --report hit_rate,avg_ttfb` -> returned `hit_rate=0.12, avg_ttfb=18ms`

jamal: Also adding a runbook note: when token p95 spikes, run kernel_variant breakdown and kv hit probe as first two steps. Will add to incidents repo.

alex: ack. @maya @linh @jamal thanks — keep updates in this thread and drop the dashboard PR link when ready. :thumbsup:

maya: ack :thumbsup:

linh: acked, will post KV audit results here.

jamal: assigning follow-ups in Jira now (INF-4210 INF-4211 INF-4212).
